Reject dangling or unapproved QMS references and direct edits of external QMS content; keep obsolete procedure versions historically readable.

An ineffective CAPA or unacknowledged correspondence must remain open; a successful report transport must not close those tasks.
A-04: Create separate individual, periodic-summary and trend report records from one scoped case register with their own approval histories.
Reject treating a PSUR as a periodic summary or treating a generic MIR test as completion of all reporting modes.
A-05: Show product PRRC responsibility and escalation owner; approve the identical package with distinct Medical and RA human identities.
Reject one account holding both approvals, workload approval and stale package scope; do not invent a third mandatory PRRC signature.
A-06: Record product/process-specific PRRC responsibility, written source and deputy; show assignments independently of application roles.
An RA role without an appointment reference must not satisfy the responsibility matrix; missing deputy remains a visible gap.
A-07: Record recall, withdrawal and conformity measures separately, with product/country recipients and simulated authority/NB notification evidence.
Reject a measure without scope or recipients and prohibit actual customer recall from the synthetic profile.
A-08: Capture an authority request with original dossier, owner, due time, response revision and complete case export.
A late response for another dossier/round must not close this request or its deadline; missing attachments block a complete-export claim.
A-09: Open and approve a TD change from a case, trend or PSUR; retain the exact originating revision through implementation evidence.
Reject completing a change with no implementation proof or overwriting its original TD revision.
A-10: Locate versioned PMS plan and report documents in Annex III structure through scoped search and original-content retrieval.
Deny unscoped full-text hits and historical downloads after product access is revoked; missing index content is not proof of no evidence.
B-01: Trace a synthetic product's signals, cases and evidence over the lifecycle using source, ingestion and awareness timestamps separately.
Duplicate source IDs must not create duplicate cases; reordered intake must not replace the first genuine awareness.
B-02: Freeze a PSUR that explicitly references its vigilance cases and FSCA revisions, including state at the period boundary.

An expectedness flag alone must not trigger the reporting exception or discard the incident from monitoring.
B-04: Use a reviewed trend signal and its trend report as explicit versioned PSUR source records.
A rejected candidate or an unapproved later trend revision must not silently replace the accepted frozen source.
B-05: Record a literature search strategy, query/retrieval date, protocol, human relevance and synthetic register provenance.
Source failure, unavailable full text or missing reuse rights must remain visible and cannot become an asserted completed literature review.
B-06: Ingest synthetic form, email/telephone transcript and distributor-channel signals with original content, provenance and reporter role.
Missing source/original and duplicate incident submissions must not become distinct acknowledged complete cases.
B-07: Read public similar-product FSN/vigilance material as comparison evidence with original source and human relevance assessment.
Reject relabeling another manufacturer's public event as a confirmed event of the fictional manufacturer or computing incidence from raw counts.
B-08: Compute product complaint/event rates with an approved matching exposure denominator, period and documented comparison population.
Reject mismatched unit, geography or period and unavailable denominators; never compare a raw count to an incidence rate.
B-09: Apply versioned problem and patient-consequence coding, separate urgency and obtain two distinct human reviews of the same evidence.
Reject unknown or retired codes without historical proof and block approval after the bound coding/evidence revision changes.
B-10: Link returned-device condition, causal investigation and field reports to a case with country/batch/user-group analysis.
Missing custody or a traceability-compromising test without prior notice/release must block the investigation effect.
B-11: Register a forwarded authority signal with its original awareness and source, then record a reasoned human non-reportability decision.
Arrival in Cohors or a later AI run must not reset the legal clock; an authority-forwarded source cannot lose its provenance.
B-12: Classify use error and information deficiency separately and create source-bound usability/IFU change requests.
Reject replacing a human causal assessment with an automatic blame label or editing approved IFU bytes in place.
C-01: Create a case with explicit incident type, problem and patient consequence using the bound controlled terminology release.
Reject absent mandatory coding, invalid hierarchy levels or unrelated release mappings without inventing a clinical consequence.
C-02: Record the human decision-tree result, rationale and cited rule revision and derive the correct reportability deadline.
An incomplete decision or AI-only suggestion must not become a binding classification or extend an existing deadline.
C-03: Accept the expected-side-effect exception only with product-information citation, quantified TD rate and trend-monitoring inclusion.

C-04: Create a third-country FSCA with explicit markets and evaluate the EU obligation when the same product is marketed in the EU.
Missing EU market evidence must remain unknown; a country-label change must not reuse approvals for another FSCA scope.
C-05: Export and validate each supported vigilance format and record simulator, Domibus stub, AS4 and playground evidence separately.
Reject unsupported contract versions and prevent real authority transmission without an approved channel and registered actor.
C-06: Calculate the standard legal deadline from bound awareness/rule/calendar and show reminders plus accountable PRRC escalation.

An absent on-call acknowledgement must escalate; successful technical alarm delivery must not count as human acceptance.

Reject using browser timezone or generic OtherSerious timing to delay the applicable urgent deadline.

Simple recoding, reclassification or a later causal opinion without new information must not restart the legal clock.

A correlation must not become established causation automatically; edits cannot overwrite original awareness or historical causal judgments.

Missing country or an unconfigured authority must block final routing rather than default to an arbitrary recipient.

G-13: Map synthetic registry survival/revision data to the correct UDI with declared schema, provenance and time basis.
Reject ambiguous UDI, unapproved real health data and interpreting an absent registry record as absence of an event.

H-05: Follow a PMS-origin design/labeling change from rationale and source through approved implementation evidence.
Reject self-approval, stale source revision and completion without proof of the actual controlled change.
